The struggle is the point.

The process of figuring things out is what teaches us, fulfills us and, in the end, makes us happy. My fear is that AI makes it easy to skip that process entirely, including when we're trying to work through our own lives.

Harvard professor and happiness expert Arthur Brooks (@arthurcbrooks) is watching more of his students use AI as a therapist. His warning: it's built to tell you what you want to hear, not what you need to hear.

The people who help us grow are the ones who care enough to be honest with us.

Who's the person in your life who always tells you the truth?

🎧 While A Bit of Optimism is on hiatus, listen to my full conversation with Arthur wherever you get your podcasts.

Excited, scared, or dead inside?

Harvard professor and happiness expert Arthur Brooks (@arthurcbrooks) says those are the three feelings your gut sends when you face a big decision, like a new job, a move, or a proposal. The right mix is 80% excitement, 20% fear, and 0% deadness.

What I love about this is that it makes a little fear a good sign. It means the decision matters.

What's your gut telling you right now?

When @gabormatemd told me this, it stopped me in my tracks…

Siblings may grow up in the same house, but that doesn’t mean their childhoods were the same. Not even close.

Same parents? Nope.
Same family? Nope.
Same childhood? Absolutely not.

Parents show up differently for each child depending on the season of their life, their relationship, and even their financial situation. 

It’s not about who is loved more.
It’s about how that love is expressed — and how each child experiences it.

If you’ve ever wondered why you and your siblings remember childhood so differently — this is why.
This clip is from my conversation with Dr. Gabor Maté on @themelrobbinspodcast 🎧 “Why You Feel Lost in Life: Dr. Gabor Maté on Trauma & How to Heal.”

You can learn more about this and so much more in his incredible book The Myth of Normal.

Just 6 years ago, my life looked very different than it does right now…and I have a video to prove it.

I was turning 52 and starting over.

Everything in my life had changed all at once.

My talkshow was canceled and I didn’t know my next career move.

My husband and I moved to Vermont and sold the home outside Boston where we had lived and raised our kids for 26 years.

I was living in a tiny town and had no friend group.

My body, my hormones, my routine and sense of self and purpose - gone.

It was almost as if I was stuck between two lives: the life I had been living and the life I had yet to create.

I started to convince myself at 52 that the best days of my life and career were behind me.

And that brings me to a video I want you to see.

It’s me on my 52nd birthday, crying alone in a bedroom describing how I feel.

Six years ago, there was no @themelrobbinspodcast .

There was no @letthemtheory book.

There was just me, starting over in a new chapter of my life and feeling scared and overwhelmed about all the unknowns.

And now here we are six years later.

Most people only know me because of what I’ve accomplished in the last four years (in my late 50s!)

You can change your life.

You can start exactly where you are and figure it out.

And if you keep waking up and moving forward and pushing yourself to try new things - over time you’ll surprise yourself.

Which is why I am waking up on my 58th birthday stunned by just how much my life has changed for the better.

If I can go from crying alone in a bedroom - to six years later changing every aspect of my life and myself - so can you.

And if you don’t believe in yourself right now, I want you to know that you can always borrow my belief in you, until you do.

Today I am doing chores in the most glamorous and expensive dress I own as a fun way to celebrate two amazing things happening this week:

1. It’s my 58th BIRTHDAY!!! (Or it was on the 6th…) - and I meant to post but I was enjoying the day with my family and never got around to it - so I’m telling you now!

2. The Mel Robbins Podcast is officially on the short list of 30 shows - who are invited to submit applications for the 2027 Golden Globes awards!!!!

In life, it is so important to stop and share good news with friends and family.

And it is also important to allow yourself to have some fun!

So, I pulled out the dress I wore as a nominee on last years red carpet (thank god it still fits) as a way to celebrate this amazing acknowledgment!

Congrats to everyone who made the Top 30!

But most importantly to all of our listeners around the world in 193 countries. Thank you for spending time with me and for sharing the episodes that inspire you with the people you love.

Keep those unpaid therapists in your life close… 

The friend who always knows exactly what to say and never judges, the coworker who can totally relate to everything you’re saying, the neighbor who notices when you need a boost…

They’re rare, they’re gold, and they deserve to know it. 

Tag your important people below ❤️

EXCLUSIVE: Leave a “YES” below and I’ll DM you the full episode with @collingosselin1👇 Colin is shareing his story like never before on On Purpose 🎙️

Millions of people watched Colin grow up on Jon & Kate Plus 8. But what the cameras captured was only one version of his childhood. For the first time, Colin shares his account of what was happening behind the scenes—including childhood abuse, isolation, being institutionalized at 11 years old, and the years he spent trying to reclaim his life.

We talk about growing up without privacy, feeling unable to ask for help, being separated from his siblings, rebuilding his relationship with his dad, and the lasting impact of having your most formative years turned into entertainment for millions of people.

What stayed with me most was the purpose Colin has found through everything he’s experienced. Rather than allowing his past to define his future, he’s determined to use his story to advocate for children who may not have the ability or opportunity to speak for themselves.

If you’ve ever felt unheard, struggled to heal from your childhood, had to rebuild trust after being hurt, or wondered how to turn the most painful parts of your story into something meaningful… I hope this conversation reminds you that your past doesn’t have to decide who you become.

I am so glad you found me! Thought it was time I re-introduced myself. 

Hi, I’m Vanessa! Welcome to my corner of the internet! 

I’m a recovering awkward person, bestselling author, lover of behavior research, mom of two, ambivert, social overthinker. I’m here to be aggressively helpful to you.

So lovely to meet you ❤️

#gettoknowme #introduction #reintroduction #contentcreator #factsaboutme

We all want 3 things: to be understood, chosen and loved ❤️

Conversation expert @vvanedwards says great conversations are one of the fastest ways to get there.

Whether it’s with your boss, your partner or someone you’ve just met, deeper conversations can help you skip the small talk and feel genuinely understood.

What’s the best conversation you’ve had recently?

Comment ‘more’ and we’ll DM you this conversation.
Never Ever Say “Nice To Meet You” | @jenniferhudsonshow

Loved this quote by @jennifer.garner on @aspirewithemmagrede 

I know I’ve found the smallest of kind gestures to make the biggest impact.

A thoughtful text. Holding the door. Checking in on someone. Letting someone merge in traffic. Complimenting a stranger. Remembering the little thing someone mentioned weeks ago.

You never really know what someone is carrying, and a tiny gesture that takes you five seconds might be the thing that makes their entire day a little lighter.

Be the reason someone leaves an interaction feeling a little more loved than they did before. 🤍

What’s a small act of kindness someone has done for you that you’ll never forget?

#Kindness #GoodPeople #DailyReminder #PositiveVibes #HumanConnection

Quick question: what do you think successful people do that the rest of us don’t?

The usual guesses are grit, a 5 a.m. alarm, or some genius-level IQ.

What I saw up close was a lot smaller than that, and a lot easier to copy. Three of the patterns are about how they think. Two are about how they treat people, especially the people who can’t do anything for them.

And every one is small enough to try in your very next conversation.

I’ll share the research behind each one. (Including the one that didn’t hold up. Yes, I’ll tell you which.)

Your pre-order of Conversation is your ticket in. Follow me, then comment “BOOK” and I’ll send you the link.

Being vulnerable and asking for things is one of my least favorite things to do. When we see people attack empathy or say things like, “The fundamental weakness of Western civilization is empathy” (Elon Musk, 2025), we should ask ourselves, “What harm, pain, or hurt do they not want us to see or feel? Who do they want to hurt, humiliate, or dehumanize without accountability?”

Based on our research over the past 25 years, creating meaningful connections and human-centered systems requires a combination of compassion and cognitive empathy. I think of compassion as the daily practice and cognitive empathy as one its most powerful tools.

We define compassion as the daily practice of recognizing and accepting our shared humanity so that we treat ourselves and others with loving-kindness, and we take action in the face of suffering.

Most definitions of compassion share a commitment to action. It’s not just feeling, it’s doing. Compassion is fueled by accepting that we’re all made of strength and struggle—no one is immune to pain or suffering. Compassion is not a practice of “better than” or “I can fix you”—it’s a practice based in the beauty and pain of shared humanity.

Most researchers agree there are at least two elements to empathy: cognitive empathy and affective empathy. Cognitive empathy, sometimes called perspective taking, is the ability to recognize and understand another person’s emotions. Affective empathy, often called experience sharing, is one’s own emotional attunement with another person’s experience.

The empathy we desperately need is understanding what someone is feeling, not feeling it for them. If someone feels lonely, empathy doesn’t require us to feel lonely too, only to reach back into our own experience with loneliness so we can understand and connect. Affective empathy, feeling something along with the person who is struggling, is a slippery slope toward becoming too overwhelmed to offer meaningful support.

Again, empathy is a tool of compassion. We can respond empathically only if we are willing to be present to someone’s pain. If we’re not willing to do that, it’s not real empathy. And the lack of real empathy is 100% a major threat to civilizations.

Thank you to @toninovvva for this powerful reminder.

This is one of my favorite @thecuriosityshop episodes. In a world where everyone and everything is fighting for our attention, our rage, and our money, we exam what makes us vulnerable to persuasion and how we can develop stronger influence literacy skills. 

It’s the best kind of collision between Adam’s, “think like a scientist” research and my work on shame and vulnerability. 

Biggest finding: 
Shame around being persuadable makes us more vulnerable to influence. Acknowledging that we are vulnerable to those reels and TikTok’s and snake oil pitches makes us more resistant! 

If you want to dive into the original research - all of the studies are cited in the show notes for the podcast. 

You can download or watch the episode now!

@adamgrant and I loved talking with @angelalduckworth about her new book, “Situated.”

Big takeaway:

“To stay motivated through the countless hours of practice that separate amateurs from experts, grit is necessary but not sufficient. The situation also matters—and to an astonishing degree:

Culture matters.
Mentors matter.
Teammates matter.
Even the objects in your personal space matter.

How you think about your goals and what you’re willing to do to achieve them depends on both you and your situation.”

I also loved our conversation about billboards - those signs we post around our spaces as reminders of what’s important. It reminds of why I like to write in a room where my children’s art is hanging. The kids’ art is my favorite art and it’s imperfect and honest. Grit is great, but I also need the environment to say, “Have fun. Just start.”

To watch or listen to the episode, head to YouTube or wherever you listen to podcasts.

To my Longhorn family: Try not to step in the bullshit left behind by small-minded people.
Stay strong. Like UT vs OSU strong. 🧡🤘🏻🤍

Priya Parker, one of my favorite thinkers and writers, is joining @thecuriosityshop this week and we’re talking about fighting! Not “dukes up” fighting but how real heat and conflict can build connection if we’re willing to learn how to do it well.

What I love about this conversation and Priya’s new book - “The Art of Fighting” - is being called to imagine a world where we unlearn and relearn what it means to gather and to disagree. And, she’s just so honest and fun!

To watch or listen to the full episode, head to YouTube or wherever you listen to podcasts.

Aaron Sandel @prof.sandel, an anthropologist and primatologist, has spent over a decade studying the Ngogo chimpanzees, witnessing one of the largest known chimp communities split into two factions.

Aaron helps Adam and I understand what chimpanzees can teach us about friendship, conflict, belonging, and human nature. He shares what he learned from watching these chimps show affection, navigate dominance hierarchies, and face the effects of division within their own community.

Aaron also reflects on what it was like to watch chimps he knew by name turn against one another, while exploring the surprising depth of bonds in this community.

If you’re trying to find me this semester, I’ll be the one sneaking into Aaron’s class at UT Austin! I have so many more questions!

To listen or watch the full episode, head to YouTube or wherever you listen to podcasts.

Celebrating Dolly has me thinking about the joy of reading books and how often I squander that pleasure by putting myself under pressure to consume pages. 

We are all craving deep reading, deep thinking, and deep connection — and these all require deep time. 

I went back this morning and re-read the interview we did with @mayasmarty and was drawn to her phrase the “privilege of focus.” 

Let’s start a spiritual book club where we read what we want, when we want, no meetings or deadlines - just a shared reframe of deep time as subversive in a world of shallow distraction, addictive scrolling, and unrelenting attention grabbing. ❤️📖❤️

Sometimes shiny is great. Sometimes it’s dangerous.

Episode available on YouTube or wherever you listen to podcasts.

"Vaynerchuk has created two successful companies; he is a bestselling author; he can command six-figure fees for speaking engagements; and he has 1.1 million Twitter followers. But he is largely unknown to the American television-viewing public. Rather, he is Internet famous. That fame happened by design and by years of meticulous planning—and it has drawn vocal critics for a style that is loud, bombastic and blatantly self-promotional. latestPosts.caption:
Some words stick with you.

Over the years, I’ve collected a few quotes that genuinely changed the way I think, work, and move through life. 💭

These are a few I still come back to, because sometimes the right words at the right time can change everything.

Swipe through, and tell me: which one do you need to hear right now? 👇

Sometimes the voice telling you to quit is wisdom. Sometimes it’s fear, doubt, exhaustion, or the discomfort of doing something that actually matters. 💭

The trick is learning to tell the difference.

Before you give up, pause. Get curious. Ask yourself what’s really going on—and what you actually want.

What's something you quit that turned out to be a blessing? Tell me in the comments. 👇

Throwing it back to my conversation with Lewis Howes. 

There’s a big difference between easy money and making money easy. 💰

In my conversation with Lewis Howes, we talked about the temptation to chase the shortcut—the next big opportunity, the get-rich-quick promise, the thing that looks like easy money.

But “easy money” can come with a very expensive lesson.

Making money easy is different. It’s about building the skills, experience, and systems that make creating wealth more sustainable over time.

Want to hear the full conversation with Lewis? Comment MONEY and I’ll send you the episode. 👇

Quick question: How many sales might you have lost when the right person landed on your website, opened your email, or saw your post…
…but your words didn’t click? 😬

Great copy isn’t about sounding clever, polished, or “professional.”
It’s about knowing how to write words that connect, persuade, and sound unmistakably like YOU.

Because in a noisy world,  writing that connects is a SUPER POWER.
And the good news? It’s a skill you can learn. 🙌

I created a FREE 7-Day Writing Class to help you do exactly that.
Comment WRITE and I’ll send it your way. 💌

And P.S. — if you’re ready to go much deeper, mark your calendar. 👀
We’ve got a VERY special Copy Cure offer coming October 12.
More soon. ✍️💖

Rewind to one of my favorite conversations. 💭

What if the thing you’ve been taught to see as a weakness is actually pointing you toward your greatest strength? 

In my conversation with Bryce Dallas Howard, we talked about how her learning disability shaped the way she sees herself, her strengths, and the way she works.

Sometimes the thing that makes you feel different can become the very thing that helps you find your path. ✨

Want to hear the full conversation with Bryce? Comment GIFT and I’ll send you the episode. 👇

Some weeks are full of wins.
Others are just about making it to the other side.

Whatever this week held for you, you made it through. And that counts. 🤍

Take a breath. Give yourself some credit. Now enjoy your weekend.

Happy October! 🍂🎃
There’s something about this time of year I just love. The summer travels wind down, the pace gets a little slower, and sweater weather gives me an excuse to cozy up and actually sit still for a minute. 😂

So I made myself an October bingo card with a few of my favorite fall things! 🎃👻🍁

What’s in store for you this October? 🍂

You keep saying “someday.”

Someday when you have more time.
Someday when the timing is right.
Someday when everything is figured out.

But here’s the thing: your life is happening today. ❤️

Don’t wait so long to start living the life you want that you forget to enjoy the one you have.

What’s one thing you’re done putting off until “someday”? 👇

Elizabeth Gilbert's new paperback, All the Way to the River, is out today! 📚✨

So we're bringing back this conversation because there are some ideas that are just too good not to revisit.

I loved this conversation with Liz. She is full of wisdom, honesty, and reminders about trusting yourself and following what feels true.

Congratulations, Liz, go grab her new paperback! ❤️
Comment READ and I'll send you the full episode.

@elizabeth_gilbert_writer

Sometimes you don’t need more answers. You need to ask yourself better questions. 🧠✨

Take a few minutes today to slow down, get quiet, and check in with yourself.

You might be surprised by what comes up when you stop looking outside yourself for the answer.

Which question made you stop and think? 👇

Your morning routine might be sabotaging your productivity before your day even starts. 📱🧠

The second you open your phone, you’re letting other people’s priorities, notifications, and noise into your brain before you’ve had a chance to focus on your own.

Try this instead: give yourself a little time in the morning before you reach for your phone.

Protect your attention. Protect your energy. And start your day on your terms. ✨

Could you go phone-free for the first 30 minutes of your day? 👇

Outside of work? 😂

I like to dance, laugh, play, explore, and enjoy the heck out of this wild little life. 💃✨

Because building a meaningful business matters to me, but so does having a life I actually love living.

Reminder: You’re allowed to be more than what you do for work. ❤️

What’s your favorite thing to do when you’re not working? 👇

You wake up and dread the Zoom call.
You refresh Stripe before lunch.
You avoid getting on camera.

My friend, it shouldn’t feel this hard.

The bottleneck? The three core pieces of your marketing aren’t working together, so everything feels like starting from scratch.

When they work as one, revenue steadies.

👇Comment TRAINING and I’ll send you my free training.

Only 1 in 20 top earners is a woman.

A new study of 145 women in the top 1% found that many of them didn’t start at the top.

latestPosts.caption:
If you chase after money, it has a funny way of avoiding you.

At least, that's what I've found in my career.

Instead, I'd much rather focus on something better:

Big, painful, miserable problems.

I started learning how to solve these problems back in 2009 in my startup days, and quickly figured out how valuable that was.

Solve one painful problem? Here's some money.
Solve another one? Here's more.
Keep solving them? Here's a boatload.

When you can save people money or time (or both) AND help them sleep better at night, you have incredible earning potential.

So work on that skill ferociously.

Here's how I do it:

1. Hypothesize

When you see a big problem, try to write down every single reason you think it might be happening. Guess. Jot every single thing you can think of.

2. Rank

Stack rank them from most likely to least likely to be the culprit. Start by cutting everything except the top 2 or 3.

3. Isolate

Starting with your most likely, figure out how to isolate your hypothesis and measure it effectively.

4. Prove or disprove

Don't guide the data. Let the data guide you. Were you right? Wrong? Talk to people as well. Qualitative and quantitative feedback are useful.

5. Install

Once you've figured out the actual fix, install it. Then move on to the next problem.

Congrats...you're on your way to being hyper valuable.

This is just one of seven incredibly important skills in entrepreneurship.

I break down this one even more, and six others, in a free guide to building valuable businesses.

Everything I learned in a decade building my one-person business to $15M in profit, compressed into a short 30-minute read.

Free at my LINK IN BIO.

#entrepreneur #business #entrepreneurship #mindset #lifestyle

The worst thing in the world is getting fired without a backup plan.

I've watched it happen to so many good people.

$200,000 take-home pay one day.
$0 the next day.

What a nightmare.

That's why planning for the worst, while working hard to prevent it, is a great 1-2 punch.

Here's what I'd recommend:

1. Make some noise

Get online daily and share how you think about your industry. Let people see your name and face and become synonymous with something.

2. Build a network

Once you've made a little noise, jump into DMs. Invite people to connect. Grab coffee. Meet on Zoom. Help people. It's all about who you know.

3. Show off your expertise

At some point, don't just make noise. Translate noise into value. What have you helped your company accomplish? Toot your own horn.

4. Collect testimonials

If colleagues, managers, and peers like your work, ask them to write a little something about it. Put it on LinkedIn. Put it on your website. Show off what other people think about you.

5. Connect people

Lastly, make mutually beneficial connections.

Once people feel like you've helped them out, they'll remember you when opportunities show up.

If you can do these five things, you'll have one hell of a backup plan.

Because now you're building assets that belong to you instead of your employer:

A reputation.
A network.
Your expertise.
Ability to create opportunities.

Do that long enough and you can probably earn extra money without depending entirely on one company.

You just have to know how to turn those assets into income.

I spent a decade figuring that out and turned it into a $15M one-person business.

I broke down the 7 exact skills you need to go from corporate to solopreneur in a new 30-page field manual.

Hundreds of articles, hours of voice notes, and interviews with 8-figure entrepreneurs summarized in a guide you can read in less than 30 minutes.

Get it free at my LINK IN BIO.

#entrepreneur #business #entrepreneurship #mindset #lifestyle

Successful people work on things that bring them joy and keep them interested.

Sure, they may do a few things that suck here and there.

But it's rare.

Take my business, for example:

- I write about what I love
- I help customers that I can benefit
- I deliver products that improve lives
- I have conversations with interesting people

All of that stuff is exciting and fun.

None of it fills me with dread, so a Monday isn't all that different than a Saturday.

So, when you're building your business, here are a few helpful questions to ask yourself:

1. What's a business I could run for decades?
2. What are tasks I definitely don't want to do?
3. What would a business make possible for me?
4. What people do I want to help succeed?

Answer them, work toward building that business, and you'll love what you do.

Now, of course, it doesn't happen overnight.

It took nearly a decade to figure out how to build a business where I did what I want, when I want, with whom I want, and very little of what I hate.

I jotted down the 7 most important skills I developed over that time and how you can develop them too.

I compressed hundreds of pieces of writing, hours of voice notes, and interviews with successful founders.

7+ years of learning in less than 30 minutes.

Read it free at my LINK IN BIO.

#entrepreneur #business #entrepreneurship #mindset #lifestyle

The problem with loyalty to a company is that it often doesn't go both ways.

So, be sure you're not working yourself to death.

Don't let work cause you to miss dinners, skip workouts, not see your family, or miss out on that vacation.

None of that stuff proves you're “committed to the mission."

And it's more important to be committed to yourself and your family.

Work hard.
Care deeply.
Do excellent work.

But don't devote your life to your work.

Your job should support your life, not the other way around.

I know a lot of folks feel like they have to do this, because they lack leverage.

So make sure you're creating some by:

- Building impressive skills that travel
- Learning how to earn income on your own
- Understanding how to promote & sell yourself 

Basically, make yourself really hard to corner.

That's how I got started building my own little one-person business.

Over 7 years, that business eventually grew to over $15M in profit.

And that became the leverage I needed to be essentially "uncontrollable."

I took the 7 most important skills for building a highly profitable one-person business and put them into a free field manual you can read.

Hundreds of articles, hours of voice notes, and interviews with successful builders compressed into something you can read in 30 minutes.

Free at my LINK IN BIO.

Read it. Apply it. And give yourself leverage.

#entrepreneur #business #entrepreneurship #mindset #lifestyle

If you want to be great at something, surround yourself with the best people.

This is why I hate most “move somewhere cheap and peaceful” advice.

It's good for 45-year-olds like me, but it's terrible for young ambitious people.

But I get it. Cheap rent's awesome.

Being the smartest guy or gal in your zip code isn't.

If you’re young and you're serious about getting insanely good at something, go where the competition scares the hell out of you.

Surround yourself with folks who are:

Making more money than you.
Building and shipping faster than you.
Taking bigger moonshots than you are.
Doing work that makes yours look mediocre.

You should start thinking, "I need to step my game up.”

It's a very useful feeling when your environment changes what feels normal.

If everyone around you is coasting, you'll coast.
If everyone around you is working hard, you will.

You can always slow down later.

But when you’re young and hungry?
Go where the competition is scary.

Then stay long enough for it to build long-lasting habits in the way you operate.

This is why I spent 10 years working in cities and companies that challenged me like crazy.

I wanted to be around high-performers who taught me how to think faster, make better decisions, and raise my standards.

I built skills that would travel with me for the next 20 years of my career and helped me build a $15M one-person business.

There are 7 skills that stand out to this day as the most important ones.

They’re the ones I’d want to learn first if I had to start over from zero today.

And one of them has almost nothing to do with selling, marketing, or productivity, but probably made me more money than any of them.

I break all 7 down in a free 30-page guide that will help you get your own one-person business started. 

Free at my LINK IN BIO.

#entrepreneur #business #entrepreneurship #mindset #lifestyle

If you want to build an incredible life, hang around incredible people.

That doesn't necessarily mean rich and successful people.

Kind people.
Interesting people.
People who lift you up.
People who normalize some form of excellence.

I've had such a wonderful time building an eclectic collection of friends.

Some are my health-nut friends, or intellectual friends, or athlete friends, or business friends.

Everyone has something interesting that they bring to the table.

A huge mistake I see people making is that they surround themselves with people who bring them down.

Complainers, whiners, life-aint-fairers.

Here's a challenge for my entrepreneur followers out there.

Find a fantastic, new, informative, high-energy business group to network with this month.

See what that does to your ambition.

Your ideas.
Your standards.
Your sense of what’s possible.

Because entrepreneurship gets a lot easier when the people around you make better decisions feel normal.

And once your standards rise, the next question is obvious:

What should you actually get good at?

I spent a decade answering that while building my one-person business to $15M in profit.

Eventually, I narrowed the biggest lessons down to 7 skills.

I broke all 7 down in a free 30-page guide on building a highly profitable solo business without letting it take over your life.

Hundreds of articles, hours of voice notes, and interviews with successful builders compressed into something you can read in 30 minutes.

Free at my LINK IN BIO.

#entrepreneur #business #entrepreneurship #mindset #lifestyle

One of the best business hacks is being your own biggest cheerleader.

Trust me, you're going to need it.

When you're just starting out, very few people will believe in you.

Maybe your spouse.
Maybe your friends.
Maybe your family.

Maybe.

So you better believe in yourself enough for all of them.

Talk confidently.
Toot your own horn.
Wear your own merch.
Celebrate the wins nobody else cares about.

You might feel a little ridiculous.

Good.

Because one day, if things work out, something funny happens:

Everyone who doubted you suddenly remembers being incredibly supportive.

"I always knew."
"I could see it coming!"

Sure.

The most important part of self-belief is that it keeps you in the game long enough to get good.

Then you *actually* have to get good.

It took me a decade to figure those things out while building my one-person business to $15M in profit.

I broke down everything I learned in a free 30-page guide to solopreneurship.

Hundreds of articles, hours of voice notes, and interviews with successful builders compressed into something you can read in 30 minutes.

Free at my LINK IN BIO.

#entrepreneur #business #entrepreneurship #mindset #lifestyle

A business that requires you all day, every day, is my personal nightmare.

I see so many entrepreneurs bragging about freedom while glued to a Slack channel, taking calls on vacation, and checking email at 5 a.m.

That’s the opposite of freedom.

A good business should make your life easier as it gets better.

More control over your time.
More money not attached to hours.
More time to be around your family.
Freedom to decide what your week looks like.

That requires some discipline. 

Because growth almost always gives you a reason to add complexity.

Another hire. 
Another offer. 
Another meeting.
Another thing you gotta manage.

You have to learn how to grow without automatically adding a ton of work to your plate.

That was one of the hardest parts of building my one-person business to $15M in profit.

Luckily, I documented a lot of it.

And turned it into a free 30-page guide on growing a highly profitable solo business without burning yourself out.

Hundreds of articles, hours of voice notes, and interviews with successful builders compressed into something you can read in 30 minutes.

Free at my LINK IN BIO.

#entrepreneur #business #entrepreneurship #mindset #lifestyle

Your 20s are probably the worst time to optimize for comfort.

You have fewer obligations, more energy, and a longer runway than you’ll probably ever have again.

Don't spend those years trying to make your life cushy.

Easy job.
Easy schedule.
Easy coworkers.
Easy expectations.

Too many people do, then they hit 35 and wonder why nobody trusts them to do something difficult.

Do the opposite.

Find people who are better than you and make yourself useful to them.

Take on some work that scares you a little.

Become the person who can be trusted with expensive, painful problems.

And then stay long enough to actually get good.

You'll build a reputation long before you desperately need one.

Because later, freedom gets much easier when you already have experience people value, people who trust you, and proof that you can deliver.

That's how I spent the first half of my career.

The second half was figuring out how to turn everything I learned into income I controlled without creating another life-consuming job.

That part took me almost another decade.

Eventually, I narrowed down the most important lessons from building my one-person business to $15M in profit.

I put them into a free 30-page guide on building a highly profitable solo business without letting it take over your life.

Hundreds of articles, hours of voice notes, and interviews with successful builders compressed into something you can read in 30 minutes.

Free at my LINK IN BIO.

#entrepreneur #business #entrepreneurship #mindset #lifestyle

Most entrepreneurs try to build a business first and then cram their life around it.

I think that's a mistake.

Before you build anything, you should decide what your business is going to make possible in your life.

Here are some important questions to think through:

How many hours do you want to work?
How much income is actually enough?
Do you want weekends protected?
Do you want employees?
Do you want meetings?
Do you want to travel?

Those answers should help shape the business model that you eventually choose.

Because the answers affect what you sell, how you price it, how much complexity you install, and what kinds of customers you avoid.

You can build a "great" business and still build the wrong one for the life you want to live.

So define your life first.
Then build the business that supports it.

That was how I approached my one-person business, and it forced me to get excellent at a handful of skills:

Choosing the best work for me.
Keeping everything overly simple.
Protecting my time (especially weekends).
Creating predictable income with automation.
And growing without adding any complexity.

I learned so many lessons building my business this way. 

I took 7 of the most important ones and broke them down in a free 30-page guide on how I built my one-person business to $15M in profit.

It's hundreds of articles, hours of voice notes, and interviews with successful friends compressed into a short guide you can read in less than 30 minutes.

Free at my LINK IN BIO.

#entrepreneur #business #entrepreneurship #mindset #lifestyle

If you're great at what you do, but nobody knows, that's a "you" problem.

The market isn't going to discover you because you deserve it.

But, of course, someone half as talented is posting their work, explaining what they know, showing results, asking for the business, and getting paid.

Being uncomfortable with self-promotion is expensive.

But you don't need to become obnoxious.

You do need to get good at three things:

1. Show your work.

Talk about what you're building, what you're learning, what worked, and what failed. Be open, honest, and helpful.

2. Make your value extremely obvious.

Explain the problem you solve and show the result. Make it simple. A 6th-grader should be able to understand it.

3. Repeat yourself daily.

You are significantly more tired of your message than everyone else is. Most people missed it, forgot it, or are new to your world. Repeat!

People can't buy work they don't know exists.

And if you're building a one-person business, nobody else is coming to create that attention for you.

You have to learn how to get attention, earn trust, make good decisions, and turn your skills into income without spending your entire life doing it.

That took me years to figure out.

I wrote down everything I learned in a free solopreneur guide.

Hundreds of articles, hours of voice notes, and interviews with successful builders compressed into something you can read in less than 30 minutes.

100% free at my LINK IN BIO.

#entrepreneur #business #entrepreneurship #mindset #lifestyle

The 24/7 grinders won't experience the joy of a relaxed weekend with their spouse.

What a tragedy.

What's the point of doing all of this work if you never get the joy of downtime?

"Rise and grind."
"I'll sleep when I'm dead."

Lol. OK.

There's nothing wrong with hard work. I love working hard.

And there's nothing wrong with the occasional all-nighter or tough week, or workaholic month.

I get that. I've been there, too.

But if your identity is that work always gets 100% of your time, you're going to be a very sad and lonely person as you age.

If I could give one piece of advice to any aspiring entrepreneur, it would be this:

Build your life first and your business second.

Envision exactly how you want to live. What do your months, weeks, and days look like?

Then, fill in the gaps with exactly how work can support it.

I wrote down 30 pages of notes on how I did exactly that, and what skills were necessary (and unnecessary) to develop over time.

You can read it free at my LINK IN BIO.

I hope you enjoy it. Cheers. 

#entrepreneur #business #entrepreneurship #mindset #lifestyle

For more than a decade, I lived the kind of life ambitious people are told to want. I helped build two companies past $1B in valuation and raised more than $300M in venture capital. By 33, I was Chief Revenue Officer at a venture-backed company, making more money than I’d ever imagined. And quietly falling apart.

I was burned out, anxious, drinking too much, and increasingly convinced that if I kept going, I might not see fifty.
Then one afternoon, in our house in Los Angeles, I had a panic attack so severe I ended up on the kitchen floor. 

My wife, Jennifer, called 911. The paramedics came.

This method from Cal Newport helped me figure out what I wanted to do with my life.

It's called values-centric lifestyle-based career planning. The idea is simple: work backwards from the lifestyle you want.

A lot of us think "I did a degree in X, so my only options are A, B, or C."

But actually, start by asking yourself what kind of life you want.

📅 What would your ideal week look like?

💸 What would you be doing if money were no object?

Most people get meaning from work. It's just that you'd probably be doing work you enjoy. So what would that look like?

Then based on that, figure out what kind of career would actually facilitate that lifestyle.

This advice really resonated with me when I was in med school.

🔍 Start with the life you want, then figure out the career that gets you there.

If you want to track where the 168-hours of your week goes, comment TIME for my free spreadsheet.

Someone asked: "My son just turned 22. What advice would you give him?"

Firstly, I don't give advice to people who aren't asking for it. So I probably wouldn't force my advice down your 22-year-old son's throat.

But if a 22-year-old came up to me and asked for general life advice, I'd say this.

When you're 22, you don't have a lot of experience in many things. You probably did something at university, maybe had some hobbies or side hustles, but you've got a fairly narrow range of stuff you've actually tried.

(P.S. Comment FOUNDATIONS below for my free 7-lesson course on how to build a $100k/year business)

So from 22 to 25, just try loads of things. Internships. Working for a small business. Random hobbies and side projects. Try learning the skills to make money independently on the internet.

And make sure you are creating more than you are consuming. Creating doesn't have to mean content. It can mean any form of making stuff and putting it out into the world.

Paul Graham has a great essay about finding work you love, and one of his guiding principles is "always be producing." The people who stumble into interesting careers tend to produce a lot. Most 22-year-olds I know spend 10 hours a day consuming content other people made.

Shift from consumer to creator. Try enough things and you'll eventually find the one where you're like "oh, I actually enjoyed that more than the others”, then narrow it down from there.

As Naval Ravikant says, find the thing that feels like play to you but looks like work to other people 🧙

latestPosts.caption: Everybody is jealous of the destination. Nobody is jealous of the journey.

5 money rules my wife and I follow as a couple aged 45 with two kids.

1. We don’t spend money to look rich. 

We spend to become wealthy and gain freedom of our time.

So, there’s no car. It’s rented. 
We own the house we live in, no other real estate.

No spending on brands. No spending just to show off to people.

2. We spend extravagantly on high-quality food.

We know that what goes into our body is ultimately the biggest wealth we have, and unfortunately, healthy food is not cheap.

3. We spend on experiences more than things.

Things give you happiness once, and they have no end.

You remember experiences, and they make you a better person. 
You grow as a person.

We travelled 116 days last year!

4. We invest before spending.

As soon as our salary comes, the largest amount is invested.

The remaining amount is used for expenses.

We are recording this on the 30th. 
₹9,000 and ₹600 left in our bank accounts. 
Everything else is invested.

5. No budget for books and learning.

No amount of money spent is enough.

Ruchi is learning pottery, watercolor painting, and tennis.

Our kids also go to many classes.

These are our rules. 
They may not apply to you, but having your own rules is important in life.

Before you say yes to marriage, check these 5 things.

1. Why are you getting married? Is it for the sake of society? Is it for the sake of your parents? Is it for your own good?

2. How do you handle fights with your partner? Because fights will continue. If you handle them properly, then relationships will progress.

3. Do you have an alignment on money and responsibility? How will you spend money? How will you share responsibilities?

4. Do you have space for your own personality? You can make friends without involving their friends. You can live your own life without depending on them.

5. How will you spend your life after marriage? What are the expectations from your family? How will your daily routines be? What will be your living arrangements? What have you thought about your children?

This is an important decision. Don't take it in a hurry.

4 signs that your life is much better than you think.

1/ Someone in your family has stopped worrying about you - because they trust you now.

2/ Your 18-year-old self wouldn't believe where you've reached.

3/ People now ask you for advice about something you once used to panic about.

4/ One bad day doesn't ruin your entire week, one bad week doesn't ruin your month, and one bad month doesn't ruin your year.

Sometimes, you've already made more progress than you realise.

There's a difference we often miss.

Being dependent means you need them to function. 
Being dependable means they can count on you, and you on them, without either of you losing yourselves.

One comes from fear. 
The other comes from strength.

The strongest relationships aren't two people who can't live without each other.

They're two whole people who choose, every day, to be someone the other can rely on.

3 reasons we bought our first home at 40 and not at 25 or 30.

1/ By the time we hit 40, we knew we wanted to live in Delhi.

At 25 or 30, there’s so much flexibility in life to change cities, even change countries if you want to.

But by the time we reached 40, we already knew we’re going to stay here. That’s why we chose this place.

2/ At that time, we had enough money that we could afford its EMI and its down payment for the house we wanted to live in.

At 25 or 30, that house wasn’t affordable for us.

3/ The house we wanted to live in is a very premium apartment.

The locality we wanted to live in, the area we wanted - we knew all of that by the age of 40.

Because we’d already had kids, life had settled.

In your 20s and 30s, life is still moving, so you don’t know how big a house you need, which locality you’ll prefer, etc.

That’s why I often say - instead of buying a house at 25 or 30, delay it a little and buy a house at the right time.

Raunak spent years struggling to get his words out.

Today, he helps others find their voice. 

A story of resilience, transformation and finding strength in his own voice 💪

Should you tell your parents how much you earn?

There’s a case for yes. They raised you, supported you, and may have every reason to know.

But there’s another side.

Once they know your salary, expectations can change - a bigger house, a car, a trip, a higher contribution at home.

So instead of telling them exactly how much you earn, you could tell them what your money can do for them.

“I can contribute ₹X towards the house.”

“I can afford this trip.”

“I can cover this EMI.”

Tell them what your money can do, not necessarily how much you make.

A counterpoint of view - do you agree?

Some people don't add to your life. 
They slowly drain it.

The ones who confuse you. 
The ones who hurt you and call it a joke. 
The ones who take your energy and give nothing back.

We keep them around out of guilt, or history, or habit.

But protecting your peace isn't cold. 
It's necessary.

You're allowed to walk away from anyone who only knows how to take.

5 questions people ask - and how we hear them.

1/ “When are you getting married?”

We hear that nothing I’ve done in life so far means nothing until I get married.

2/ “How much do you earn now?”

We hear that my entire worth is based on one salary, one number, and that will give me a rank.

3/ “Sharma ji’s son, well…”

We hear that I will never be enough. Someone else will always be doing better than me.

4/ “You studied so much and you’re doing this?”

We hear that if I make my own choices in life, that will never be accepted.

5/ “You’ve gotten a little healthy.”

We hear that we’re meeting after a year and the first thing anyone sees is my body.

They must think that they care about you, they care for you.

But the way we receive it is what our mind tells us.

When a child is punished for the truth, they don’t stop doing the thing.

They just get better at hiding it.

Fear doesn’t build honesty. 
It builds distance. 
It teaches a child that the safest option is to never let you see who they really are.

The kids who grow up telling their parents the truth aren’t the ones who were scared into it.They’re the ones who knew the truth was safe.

This will be a slightly controversial take.

Living in Mumbai on ₹1 lakh a month, or at your home, your village, your city, ₹60,000 a month.

Many people will say the financially right decision is to stay at your home. 
There’s no rent, work-life balance is much better, and expenses are lower.

I say, live in Mumbai.

Live in Mumbai for the first five years of your life.

Absorb the energy of that city.

Meet people.

Go into those rooms that scare you to enter.

Because by the time you turn 35, your network will handle everything.

But at 35, you won’t build your network again.

Would you agree?

profile.headline: Founder @WebVeda, @IndiaGeniusChallenge @Monzy • 6X Bestselling Author • 16M+ community
profile.summary: Ankur is a prolific entrepreneur, author, and content creator dedicated to empowering others through education, personal growth, and financial literacy. Driven by a deep mission to help people make conscious life choices from a point of awareness rather than ignorance, he balances an intense startup-building schedule with continuous learning and family life. In a relationship, he would bring a strong commitment to shared responsibilities, clear communication, personal autonomy, and investing heavily in experiential memories and mutual growth.

latestPosts.caption:
IG, it’s been a while! 👋 I took a step back to focus on @getsuperboba & my YouTube channel, but recently someone asked me why I don’t share more about how I’m managing all the things. 
The truth is, I have a lot of things I love & do, and that’s exactly why I find it harder to post here. I kept feeling like none of it fit together. There is no “niche.” 
But I’m reminded that IS the niche: Who I am, how I live, what I’m building. Some business, some fitness, some productivity, some content tips, some faith, and whatever else I’m into. 
So if you want to see MY version of founder life, follow along! 
PS: What do you actually want to see more of? Let me know in the comments below!! IM BACK BABY 🧋
@leonlarano said lock in so we locking in fr 🔒

Decided to start a weekly founder diary as a place to just share the things I’m experiencing! Expect a new episode every Monday 🤸🏻 
I’m starting this series bc I often feel alone in some of my problems. 
For example, because I mainly do content for Superboba, when I’m networking with e-commerce founders, I often feel like I’m not ecomm enough because I’m not in the weeds of our operations the way that Leon is. I don’t talk ROAS, supply chain, and margins the way they can. 
But then, when I’m in creator circles, I also don’t feel creator enough because our KPIs and priorities are so different. 

I’m not super concerned about views or the latest creator hacks - I’m thinking about how to attract the right customers for my physical product, while still keeping my personal brand running. 
At the same time, running an ecom biz is SO CASH INTENSIVE! Especially if you’re scaling it, you’re putting every dollar back into the biz!! 

So what helps is tapping into my other income streams, but I’ve been getting feedback from brands about my positioning has also been confusing - the lifestyle ones think my audience is too business, and the business ones think my content is too lifestyle 🫩 can’t a girl just post her life!?

Anyways, right now I feel like I’m in the middle of everything…

But instead of feeling discouraged, I trust that the way I want to position myself on here takes one post at a time, and my goal with this founder diaries is for you guys to see ALL of it and know that life and business isn’t just one dimensional. 

Anyways, stay tuned for more weekly diaries here of snippets of my life and let me know if you’re excited for this series OR if you resonate with anything I mentioned in this week’s entry! 🍵❤️

Exactly 1 year ago, I sat at my @alphacourse group table and confessed that I was scared to share my faith journey publicly.

Honestly, I was even scared to call myself a Christian, because I still had so many doubts and questions. 
But then I started thinking about: 
1. All the coaches I’ve worked with, and how quick I was to glorify them on my platforms (sometimes too soon, and before they’d even delivered what they promised). 
2. All the concerts and festivals I’ve been to, some for artists I didn’t even know, and how fast I was to dance, sing, and post about it (even when I wasn’t a fan of the music). 
3. All the products I’ve promoted with zero hesitation: beauty, tech, clothing, software, gyms. 
So I had to ask myself: why wasn’t I doing that for God? 
That realization is what got me to start sharing my faith more. EVEN with questions. EVEN while I’m still learning. 
Because one thing I know for sure is that God has renewed my perspective on life. 
I get a lot of comments saying I’m “glowing,” that I seem “happier,” that my energy is “different,” that I can “hold so much.” 
It’s all because of God, and because of walking alongside others who believe in Him. 
He’s the one who kept me grateful when I felt alone in my problems. He’s the one who reminds me to let go of what I can’t control and trust the plan He has for me. 
So if you’re reading this and you’re scared to share, just know that I am too!   But if we can be loud about everything else we love, we can be loud about Him too.

“I’m not a runner” became “I hate running” and then “I don’t run”  Same with

“I suck at short form —> “I hate short form” —> “I don’t post short form”

Or  “I suck at vlogs” —> “I hate vlogs” —> “I don’t post vlogs” 
Things that I sucked at became things that I hated, and then into things I avoided.  The issue with this is then I would’ve never proven to myself that I CAN. 
Training for Hyrox is forcing me to question all labels I’ve put on myself and I now wonder:  “If I was wrong about this, what else have I decided I “can’t” do?” 
A month ago I could barely run for 10 minutes. 

Now I’m running 3 to 4 times a week, and my 5K pace has gone from 7:40 to 5:54 (!!!)

It’s stretching me, and it’s not comfortable. 

But I’m grateful, because the mental strength I’m building on these runs is showing up everywhere else and I’m genuinely excited for what the next 3 months has in store for me! 
Sooo that my experience as a “non runner” and ask yourself:   What’s a label you’ve been carrying that might not be full on CAP?? 🧢

Today the whole fam sensed my crash out and pulled up to support. Rare aesthetic to have all 7 of us in one room 🤣

Q4 means a handful of brand partnership deliverables, @getsuperboba BFCM prep, Hyrox training, and just girl things - I was at my limit today but grateful for my fam 😩🩸

The best business idea I ever had came from a bad habit. 
4 years ago, whenever I was craving an escape from the stresses of running a business, I’d immediately go on UberEats and order myself a bubble tea. 
After repeating this habit for months, on top of other poor lifestyle choices, I gained over 15lbs. 
Then came my big burnout, and with it a wakeup call to turn my health around, including being more mindful of what I’m putting in my body. 
I made so many healthy swaps, but still couldn’t find a proper replacement for boba. 
So my husband and I went searching for a solution, and started a business around it. 
Today, whenever I’m craving boba, I just prepare our @getsuperboba Super Pearls :) 
Super Pearls are designed to absorb any sweetener you soak them in, with zero cooking required. 
Here I added monk fruit (a zero calorie sweetener) to some warm water, soaked the pearls for 2 mins, and they turned out delicious. 
I pair them with our Superboba teas, which have adaptogens (Lion’s Mane, Maca, and Reishi) to support energy, mood & focus 🤎 
You don’t always have to go looking for a big idea. 
If there’s a problem in your life you keep waiting for someone else to solve, that might be your sign to roll up your sleeves and go find the solution yourself!

For years I waited for a sign that I was making the right call. A number, a validation, someone telling me “yes, this will work.” 
It never came first. Proof only showed up AFTER I’d jumped. 
Sign up for that competition. Try that new hobby. Start that business. Publish that video!!! ROOTING FOR YALL 🫶

One of the hardest parts of running AI agents has turned out to be deciding when they should interrupt you.

If they check in too often, you've built a very expensive notification system. 
If they check in too rarely, you find out Thursday about something that went out Tuesday.

So start by sorting the work by one question: how bad is it if the agent gets it wrong? If its…

1️⃣ Easy to undo, nobody notices: let it handle it (archiving newsletters, declining cold pitches)
2️⃣ Easy to undo, but it goes out in your name: have it draft and wait for your yes (client replies, anything that books your time)
3️⃣ Hard to undo: have it bring it straight to you (money, legal, anyone you know personally)

As the drafts keep coming back good, things move up a bucket.

Thanks again to Brian Sozzi and the Yahoo Finance team for having me. If you want the full clip, follow and comment YAHOO and I'll send it over.

Meta just put a personal AI agent one tap away from every Instagram user (top right corner of your profile), and it's very easy to hit "allow" without reading a word.

Muse reads your Gmail and calendar, searches the web for you, texts you back with a thumbs-up emoji, and has a tab literally labeled "soul and memory".

Here's the mega-quick setup, plus my rule for any new agent: read the permissions (Muse can't delete your email, which I love), give it a boring first job like auditing your subscriptions, and only hand over more access once it's earned it.

And if you want the full setup, follow and comment MUSE to get the video 🤘

You don’t need better prompts. You just need to stop typing them.

Codex voice mode takes about 10 minutes to set up. After that you just talk, and it does the work on your computer. Swipe for the step-by-step and the exact things I say to it. Save this so the steps are handy.

Follow and comment VOICE and I’ll send you the full guide 🔗

Stop prompting AI every morning.

Instead, start setting up proactive agents (like Meta Muse, Instinct, or OpenAI Dots) so that it goes out, finds the information, and brings it back to you proactively.

The initial set up looks like: giving them your goals, linking your email, docs and meeting notes, and handing each one a job. From there, they flag things back to you without you prompting.

When you DO need to ask for something, keep it loose. My last prompt simply said "HALP" with two screenshots and it took over my computer to fix the issue while I watched.

These models are strong. Give them room.

Comment: MILLIONS //Get access to a free *no-pitch* training that will help you develop a mindset to build a business worth millions.

In the simplest terms, I’d focus 100% on WHO I was selling to, and less about the specifics of WHAT.

Once you know who you want to help (new moms, students applying to college, single dads of toddlers, etc), figuring out what to sell to becomes easier once you understand what they need.

Here’s my 4-part advice:
1.  Learn how to craft an offer my dream client ACTUALLY want to buy
2. Post on social media with content that helps them (you don’t need lots of views or vitality…just tailor make it for them!)
3. Use DMs to have authentic conversations so people know me, like me, trust me, and (easily) buy from me
4. Iterate everything so I can build a SYSTEM for sustainable revenue

If you’d like to watch a free 12-minute training learning more about my method, comment:
METHOD
😘

My father is a Mexican immigrant.  He lives with legs in two different worlds: 1. Blindly patriotic to America and wears a USA flag pin on his lapel most days; and 2. Carrying the weight of memories from a different country where much was taken.

He raised me to believe that education is the most valuable thing in which I could invest.

Why? On the surface, you’d think he loved the constant pursuit of knowledge (he’s the type of guy who’ll casually slip in 10-syllable words over breakfast chilaquiles), but it’s truly about owning something that can never be taken from you.

I deeply believe the same.

I invest 10% into ongoing education/personal development every year and it’s profoundly changed my business.

If you’re a regular listener of my podcast (or you watch on YouTube), you heard me admit that I’ve hit a creative rut.

That’s extraordinarily hard for me to admit, but it’s true.

Creating content (something that used to sprout from my mind like dandelions) suddenly required a Herculean effort. It felt like I was trying to create in a parched desert.

It started in October 2022. And here we are in October 2026.

FOUR YEARS IN A CREATIVE DEATH VALLEY?!?

On the outside, it’d be hard for you to tell, but on the inside? Exhausted. What once gave me energy, was now sucking it all away.

(Continued in the comment below ⬇️)

Why do I talk like I’m mad?! 🤔 I swear, it’s PASSION. A deep desire to empower women to make money… 

…by simply having a conversation.

You have a solution. They have a desire/problem/need.

A simple conversation via Direct Message can change their life, and yours. 

Social media has changed and even though there are many longing for once was, the reality is that it’s even more powerful…

The question remains whether we are willing to do what it takes to harness its power in the new social landscape. 

In light of this, let’s start simple: let me know what you sell or where you’re located so we can chat in the comments and get to know each other better!
Quite possibly the MOST annoying sound. Ever. 😆
Did your high school math teacher lie to you?

The Art of Not Being Ready AND DOING IT ANYWAY Will Take You Very Far.

On a scale of 1 (not) - 10 (most), how ready are you?  I’ll go first: -3 😜 

Quote: @drcarolineleaf

Want a bigger business?  DO LESS.
What’s one thing you can stop before end of year?

Insider Look: How I quickly send DMs…and how you can use DMs to grow your business.

Direct messages are the future of sales.

When everybody is using automation, it’s time for you to go highly personalized.

(When they zig, you better zag!)

In this example video, not only am I showing how I respond to direct messages…

I’m also explaining how you can use them in your business to drive sales and revenue

So how many direct messages will you send today?

Oh, September, I asked to leave behind what didn’t serve me…and you took me literally with emergency surgery. 

And despite it all, I’m thankful.

So, so thankful. 

Shall we begin in reverse order of this rollercoaster of a month?

1. After two visits to the ER in three days, surgery was scheduled. Not on our Bingo card. 
2. Refusing to let my health damper our love, we celebrated our anniversary at home with sushi.
3. The flu took me down for four days, but devoured amazing books.
4. God, and goodness.
5.  Went to Guadalajara, Mexico for stem cells.
6.  Sometimes dinner at your parents’ house is all you need.
7.  First day of school.
8.  Our happy place.
9.  That Bonnie and Clyde type love.
10.  The single best thing to happen to our lives. Ever. 

If I had to use one word to describe the month, it’d be: HEALING.

Unexpected healing. 

Okay that was two words. I blame the pain killers 😉 

What’s a word you’d use?

Entrepreneurs decide their way of thinking, and resist feelings that cloud their beliefs. What do you believe is possible for your business?

Less feelings, more facts, take action, get results. 

You would not be given the vision if you didn’t have the capacity to bring it to life.

Dessert that’s yummy AND gives me my protein fix? 
Now that’s a WIN WIN 🤎😋

Ingredients:
• 1/2 cup almond flour
• 1/2 cup Yogabar's chocolate protein powder
• 1/4 cup smooth peanut butter
• 1/4 cup honey 
• 1 tbsp melted coconut oil
• 1 tsp vanilla extract
• pinch of sea salt
• 1/4 cup chocolate chips
• flaky sea salt, for topping 

Method: 
• Mix peanut butter, honey, melted coconut oil & vanilla until smooth.

• Add almond flour, protein powder & sea salt. Mix into a soft dough.

• Fold in half the chocolate chips and press into a thin layer on parchment.

• Melt the remaining chocolate chips, spread on top & finish with flaky sea salt. 

• Freeze until firm, then break into pieces.

• Store in the fridge or freezer. If frozen, let it soften for a few minutes before eating.

When I started my journey over 14 years ago as a personal trainer and running bootcamps in the park, I never imagined that one day I would have my own fitness and nutrition app that would help millions of people all over the world start their fitness journey’s 🙌

And I definitely never imagined that I would have my own TV ad ☺️

Tonight on ITV, my brand new TV advert for the Body Coach App goes live. I hope you like it ☺️

Comment below if you’ve ever tried my workouts or recipes? 💙
My 10 year overnight success story 🙌

This is a really special moment for me ❤️
 
I’ve spent the past 8 years visiting schools, leading workouts for kids, and doing everything I can to get children moving and feeling good. From school tours to PE with Joe, I’ve seen how powerful a bit of movement can be - not just for physical health, but for confidence, mood, and mental wellbeing.
 
Now, after more than 2 years of love, energy and hard work, I’m so proud to finally share something brand new with you…

It’s called Activate 🎉
 
Activate is a FREE animated workout series designed to get kids moving, laughing and having fun this summer — and beyond. 

You’ll meet my Activator gang and dance to amazing music powered by @umusicuk, and feel the joy that comes from moving your body.
 
This has been created in partnership with the amazing team at @studioaka (the legends behind Hey Duggee) and supported by @dhscgovuk @educationgovuk and @dcmsgovuk to help make movement more accessible for all families and schools across the country.
 
🎬 The first episode is LIVE now on my YouTube channel — hit the link in my bio to check it out and get your little ones moving with us.
 
Please share it, tag your videos with #ActivateWithJoe, and let’s spread the joy of movement to as many kids as we can 🙌
 
Let’s get the next generation moving ❤️

latestPosts.caption:
I hate dupes and I never thought I’d be collecting dupes but when it came to destroying perfectly good clothing I had no choice but to save them. 

With THOUSANDS OF DUPES piled up at my warehouse (of which I have to pay extra for storage) I now had a different problem 🥲

That’s when I reached out to my friends and incredible fashion designers @transformationsbytracy and @kianabonollo to see if they wanted to help me do something cool with the dupes…and that’s how the @popflex_active Upcycle Project was born!

I am BEYOND MINDBLOWN at what Tracy and Kiana did with the fabric! Like 🤯🤯🤯 

If you sew and wanna take a stab at making these dresses yourself, go on the POPFLEX site and search for the DIY Upcycle Kits! You’ll get the digital pattern and I’ll also send you all the fabric you’ll need to complete your dress (cuz pls help me clear the warehouse!!) 

100% of all profits from your purchase will go directly to Tracy and Kiana because this project isn’t just about taking a stand against dupe culture, it’s about STANDING UP for independent designers too.

I hope to have more good legal updates for you this year! 🤞

latestPosts.caption:
Today is World Mental Health Day. And we’ve made great progress in recent years raising awareness and opening up the conversation about mental health.

This year, I hope we take it one step further: mental health is brain health. A growing body of research shows how our brain health connects to everything from daily brain fog and anxiety to long-term cognitive decline.

So here’s a Microstep to try today: take a moment to check-in with your own mental health by naming the feeling you’re having right now in one word. Simply putting a feeling into words can help calm the brain’s stress response.

It might be “overwhelmed.” Or “tired.” Or “uncertain.”

Whatever it is, naming it is a small way to build the muscle of self-awareness, one of the most powerful tools we have for our mental and brain health.

AI keeps pulling off things that used to be impossible. In my latest On My Mind newsletter, I write why we shouldn’t lose sight of the eight “wonders of life,” as coined by @UCBerkeleyOfficial professor Dacher Keltner, that create everyday moments of awe: moral beauty, movement, nature, music, visual design, spirituality and religion, big ideas, and life and death.

Plus, dispatches from @Dreamforce, the @LucasMuseum, and my own home, where I recently hosted an event that captured the possibility of this moment when it comes to brain health.

You can read my newsletter at the link in bio.

Wise words, whether we’re elite athletes competing at the highest levels or building healthy habits in our daily lives. Congrats to @CaitlinClark22 — @WNBA Comeback Player of the Year! — on a great season, and thank you for your deep commitment to helping people live healthier lives by putting a spotlight on healthy behaviors, including the role of exercise as one of the most powerful preventative medicines, and reminding us all to start how we can.

@OpenAI solved a problem mathematicians have wrestled with for a quarter century.

@GoogleDeepMind mapped every possible mutation hiding in our genes. These are awe-inspiring feats of the machines.

In my latest piece for @time, I write about why, even as we marvel at AI’s capacity, we shouldn’t lose sight of something irreplaceable: human-generated awe.

Dacher Keltner, professor of psychology at the @ucberkeleyofficial, looked at 2,600 stories of awe across 26 countries. He found that what most commonly led people to feel awe wasn’t nature, or spirituality, or technology — it was watching other people be kind, brave, or strong.

He calls it "moral beauty" and 95% of it comes from witnessing actions people take on behalf of others. Collective movement. Nature. Music. Visual design. Spirituality. Big ideas. Life and death. These are the other wonders Keltner found that inspire awe — and they’re all deeply shaped by human connection.

AI will keep astonishing us. But the awe that has the most profound impact is the awe we derive from each other. And as Keltner writes, that awe is available to us "if we just take a moment and wonder."

You can read my full piece at the link in bio.

As @ariannahuff pointed out, our generation rarely talked about menopause when we were younger. But we’re shouting it from the rooftops now, because women deserve better—not only from the health care system, but from their workplaces too. #menopauseawarenessmonth 

Read more about the @gallup x @pivotaldotcom survey on women’s health at the link in my bio.

“The more we share…the more we can accelerate the shift in the culture.” Couldn’t agree more, @ariannahuff.

Thanks for a great conversation on the need to make women’s health more visible.

Arianna Huffington (@ariannahuff) has a message for the people in Silicon Valley who think they are building God.

Watch or listen on Futurology. Link in bio.

What a beautiful story of hope in The @Guardian. Twenty-one years ago, a field in Norfolk was home to a single crop. Today, it is a wildflower meadow with more than 150 plant species. Since 2011, the only maintenance has been one hay cut each summer. The cut keeps the field from becoming woodland and gives more delicate wildflowers room to grow.

As @UCL Professor Carl Sayer put it: “Sometimes we’re not patient enough.” And after watching the meadow become more biodiverse each year, he says, “It’s hope — we can recover things. We just need to do less in the recovery process.”

Life is a dance between making it happen and letting it happen. In this meadow, making it happen means one simple act of care each year. Letting it happen means trusting nature and giving it time. The same is true in our lives: our daily choices around sleep, food, movement, stress and connection give our bodies and minds the support they need to renew.

Read more in The Guardian at the link in bio.

Congratulations @ArielEmanuel on the publication of Roll the Calls!

Of course I knew Ari had an amazing story. Angry boy from Chicago overcomes severe dyslexia, rises from mailroom to C-suite, transforms himself into one of the legendary dealmakers and visionaries in Hollywood history – I expected Ari’s memoir to be a page-turner. But I didn’t expect such tenderness, such sweetness, so much heart. I wasn’t ready for all the wisdom about mental health and self-confidence and resilience and the search for one’s true happiness. I simply wasn’t prepared for Shoe Dog meets Goodfellas with a dash of The Little Prince. What a pleasant, refreshing, and wonderful surprise this book is.

And that’s my blurb for the book! You can get a copy at the link in bio.

Looking back at two great days at @Dreamforce. @Salesforce’s chief marketing officer @ErinOles moderated a conversation with @officiallymcconaughey and me about who shapes culture in the age of AI.

Here’s what nobody wants to admit about the content explosion: the bottleneck was never production. It was always judgment. For most of history, we assumed the hard part was making things — and the machines have now solved that. Anyone can generate a screenplay, a song, a strategy deck in seconds. But Matthew put his finger on what the machines haven’t solved: AI can tell you what’s popular, but it doesn’t yet have an ear for what’s really good.

Those are profoundly different things. Popularity is a pattern in the data. Good is a judgment — and judgment is built from everything that never shows up in training data: taste formed over decades, failures metabolized into instinct, the thousand small refinements of a lived life. Erin compressed it into one line: the real AI superpower isn’t the tool, it’s the taste.

Which means we’ve been worried about the wrong scarcity. The scarce resource of this era isn’t intelligence — machines have made intelligence abundant. It’s wisdom. And here’s the inconvenient truth about wisdom: it can’t be generated, downloaded, or scaled. It has to be lived into existence, one experience at a time.

Machines gather knowledge exponentially. Humans gather wisdom slowly. Whether that gap becomes a crisis or a renaissance depends entirely on whether we treat our own development as seriously as we treat the technology’s. And keeping people at the center of the AI conversation was the focus of my session at Dreamforce with chief people officer Nathalie Scardino and HR leaders from around the world.

A beautiful evening celebrating the opening of the @LucasMuseum of Narrative Art — a museum as expansive, surprising and impossible to categorize as the works it celebrates.

The museum houses the art collection of George Lucas and @MellodyHobson. At a time when AI dominates our public conversation, it’s a reminder that machines aren’t the only ones producing wonders. It’s a cathedral of wonder and awe, human creativity, storytelling and connection. As Mellody said, “Narrative art creates an emotional connection, not an intellectual one.”

The museum looks, appropriately, like a spaceship, rising, curving and folding into the landscape – in fact, there isn’t a right angle anywhere in the building. Works associated with empires and religious traditions live alongside illustrations, comic strips and movie images that have shaped our lives. There is even an immersive reproduction of the Sistine Chapel ceiling, which George calls “God’s comic book” because its panels tell a story. And throughout, cinema is treated not as something separate from art history but as another chapter in our ancient drive to turn experience into narrative. It’s why one of the museum’s theaters is named for Robert Flaherty, a pioneer of documentary filmmaking.

And then there are the monsters. The museum’s exploration of them brought to mind what Guillermo del Toro’s work shows about monsters being revealing mirrors. We create them to give form to what frightens us and to explore the parts of ourselves we can’t always confront directly. The same is true of the myths, which let us wrestle with the same big questions at a larger scale. The characters and settings change but the elemental questions remain: Who are we? What do we fear? What are we willing to fight for? And who can we become?

At a moment when so much is pulling us apart, George Lucas and Mellody Hobson have created a home for the images, stories and myths that unite us — a place where art is an invitation to feel, wonder and see ourselves in one another.

As we mark World Alzheimer’s Day, more than 7 million people over age 65 in the US are living with Alzheimer’s disease — a figure that is projected to almost double in the next few decades. And more than 12 million people are caregivers to loved ones with Alzheimer’s or other dementias. There’s no sugarcoating a disease that results in the widespread loss of brain function, and no number that captures the heartbreak of seeing a loved one decline. And yet, there is reason for hope.

That’s because research shows that Alzheimer’s-related brain changes can begin up to 20 years before symptoms set in, highlighting the importance of investing in our brain health and addressing modifiable risk factors throughout adulthood.

This is a 20-year window of opportunity. As with so many chronic conditions, research is showing that with brain health, our DNA is not necessarily our destiny. We have more power than we previously thought to shape our brain health, both day-to-day and in the long run.

Read more in @incmagazine at the link in bio.
